scoring: build_effect = tests baseline of the solver that gets only this lever wrong; real_effect = mean points lost on this lever's checks in real runs

levers.name: Hidden composition of documented rules
levers.mechanism: instruction.md documents 8-15 rules for a tool (e.g. a config merger or ledger reconciler) plus an explicit precedence/combination table; visible examples exercise each rule alone; hidden tests combine 2-4 rules and hit their error paths.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents build locally correct per-rule handlers and test each rule in isolation; interactions and rejection paths are left unexercised.

levers.name: Audit-and-repair of a broken multi-stage pipeline against a documented contract
levers.mechanism: Ship a 4-6 stage data or build pipeline with 5-8 independent defects of different kinds (logic, ordering, unit, concurrency, silent truncation). Only the end-to-end contract and per-stage contracts are documented, never the bug list.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents fix the first visible failure and stop; downstream defects are masked by upstream ones; silent defects produce plausible output.

levers.name: Algorithmic lift on a size ladder
levers.mechanism: Provide a correct but naive reference program and the exact input sizes and time limit per size. Small and medium sizes pass with library-level speedups; the largest needs a reformulation (incremental update, different data structure, decomposition). Output must match the reference exactly.
levers.why_models_fail: Models apply surface-level speedups (vectorise, Numba, better call) and anchor on the given structure; the needed reformulation is an insight.

levers.name: Stacked orthogonal artifact constraints
levers.mechanism: Ask for one artifact (binary, package, container layer, dataset) that must meet 4-5 independent written constraints at once, e.g. reproducible byte-identical output, pinned versions, a size cap, a target platform, no network at runtime.
levers.why_models_fail: Each extra constraint multiplies the dependent work; models drop or rationalise away the costliest one.

levers.name: Dependent multi-stage chain with no shortcut
levers.mechanism: 8-12 stages where each stage needs the verified output of the previous one (e.g. recover a parameter from stage-1 data, which decodes stage-2 input, ...). All procedures are documented; no stage can be done out of order.
levers.why_models_fail: Errors compound across dependent steps and an early wrong value poisons later steps; success falls with coherent length.

levers.name: Format-only validator plus self-verification burden
levers.mechanism: Provide a validator that the instruction states checks format only. Correctness criteria (invariants, totals, cross-file consistency) are written in the spec and must be checked by the agent itself.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents treat a passing validator as done and submit unchecked (premature completion).

levers.name: Mixed feasible and infeasible instances with certificates
levers.mechanism: A batch of scheduling or allocation requests under written constraints; some are provably infeasible. Feasible ones need a valid (or optimal) plan; infeasible ones need a minimal conflicting subset as certificate.
levers.why_models_fail: Models invent a plan for unsolvable instances and rarely prove infeasibility.

levers.name: Documented quiet failure in a provided component
levers.mechanism: A provided library or CLI has a man page that documents a behaviour on certain input classes (e.g. returns a sentinel, truncates at a limit). Inputs contain such cases; correct output requires handling them.
levers.why_models_fail: Silent wrong outputs are propagated; agents do not read the full tool doc or check outputs.

levers.name: Small set of interacting ad-hoc rules with precedence
levers.mechanism: 15-30 non-commonsense rules (written, numbered) with an explicit precedence order, applied to a batch of cases via a stateful tool where some actions are single-use.
levers.why_models_fail: Models fall back on common-sense priors over written ad-hoc rules and miss single-use/collect-first constraints.

levers.name: Parameter identification within a documented model family
levers.mechanism: The spec fully defines a parameterised family of behaviours; the agent observes outputs of an instance and must recover its parameters, then predict outputs on hidden scenarios.
levers.why_models_fail: Requires designing experiments and generalising beyond the observed scenarios.

levers.name: Budget planning for a documented expensive job
levers.mechanism: The stated time budget and hardware make the naive full recompute impossible; the agent must cache, reuse or compute incrementally.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents ignore run-time cost and time out while busy.

levers.name: Misleading first hypothesis in a debugging task
levers.mechanism: The first symptom suggests a common cause; later evidence (logs, a second test) contradicts it; the real cause is documented system behaviour.
levers.why_models_fail: Stubborn early assumptions; ignoring contradictory information.

levers.name: Optimality gap scoring on structured instances
levers.mechanism: Large combinatorial instances with exploitable structure; generic ILP/brute force is too slow at the top size; score by gap to the oracle's optimum.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents reach for generic solvers or greedy heuristics and miss the structure.

levers.name: Beat a fully documented fixed opponent or checker
levers.mechanism: A deterministic opponent (bot, filter, compressor bound) with full source provided; the agent must produce a strategy that beats it on hidden seeds.
levers.why_models_fail: Needs creative or adversarial reasoning and experimentation, not pattern-following.

levers.name: Novel fully specified formalism
levers.mechanism: A new small DSL or VM with complete written semantics; the agent implements it and uses it to produce artifacts; hidden tests mix features and error cases.
levers.why_models_fail: Lower prior familiarity; composition and error semantics.

levers.name: Error-path and rejection weight
levers.mechanism: Spec lists which inputs must be rejected and with which code; at least 25% of hidden weight is on invalid inputs.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents optimise for the happy path; rejection is where a strong compiler still failed.

levers.name: Spec-legal input variants in combination
levers.mechanism: The input format spec allows several variants (quoting, encodings, line endings, optional fields); hidden inputs combine them.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents test on the examples given and miss combined variants.

levers.name: Coupled multi-module change in an original mid-size codebase
levers.mechanism: An original 10-30k LOC codebase; the feature touches many modules with shared invariants.
levers.why_models_fail: Success falls with files touched and engineering complexity.

levers.name: Stateful protocol with irreversible steps
levers.mechanism: A local server with a documented protocol where some actions are irreversible and order matters; the agent must plan before acting.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents act before collecting all needed information.

levers.name: Interactive program driving as a secondary ingredient
levers.mechanism: One stage requires operating a documented interactive program (REPL/TUI) where the state persists.
levers.why_models_fail: Agents stall on interactive tools.
